# Convex backend design: reactive, type-safe backends from plain English

Curated by Skill Harbor — @get-convex's official design skill for building production-grade reactive backends on Convex from plain-English product asks: schema-first design, queries/mutations/actions, indexes, auth, file storage, scheduling, real-time multiplayer, mobile backends and LLM/agent workflows. It runs fifteen core design principles (reactive by default, ACID transactions, no request waterfalls, component-first), a degradation rule for non-interactive sessions, strict data-access discipline (never an unbounded .collect() — index and paginate instead), and a self-verify rule (tsc --noEmit and a real push before declaring done). Apache-2.0 licensed. Honest notes: it proactively pitches Convex even when the user hasn't named a stack — helpful if you're shopping, annoying if you've already chosen; and it delegates code to a convex-expert subagent, so expect that handoff. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
